headline_marked: Historic win: [[Bangladesh beats Australia by 9 wickets]] in Darwin Test
headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beats Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin Test
summary: The victory marks Bangladesh's first-ever Test win on Australian soil, described by former captain Akram Khan as the country's biggest achievement in the five-day game.
details: Bangladesh secured a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, sealing the win inside four days. This marks the team's first-ever Test victory on Australian soil and only their second win against Australia in Test cricket.

The foundation was laid by fast bowler Hasan Mahmud, who took a career-best 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 in the first innings. The batting lineup then dominated, with Tanzid Hasan scoring his maiden Test century to help the team score over 400 runs.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz also provided crucial contributions to the batting effort. The victory was particularly remarkable as the team had been bowled out for 54 in a warm-up match just days earlier.
Former captain Akram Khan and BCB president Tamim Iqbal praised the team's complete performance, with Tamim calling the win 'extraordinary' and giving the full credit to the players.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team on a video call, while fans across the country celebrated the win as a national festival.
Former spinner Abdur Razzak noted that this victory strengthens Bangladesh's case for more Test opportunities against Australia in the future.
caption:
A historic first! Bangladesh has just thrashed Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.

Bangladesh secured a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, sealing the win inside four days. This marks the team's first-ever Test victory on Australian soil and only their second win against Australia in Test cricket.

The foundation was laid by fast bowler Hasan Mahmud, who took a career-best 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 in the first innings. The batting lineup then dominated, with Tanzid Hasan scoring his maiden Test century to help the team score over 400 runs.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz also provided crucial contributions to the batting effort. The victory was particularly remarkable as the team had been bowled out for 54 in a warm-up match just days earlier.

Former captain Akram Khan and BCB president Tamim Iqbal praised the team's complete performance, with Tamim calling the win 'extraordinary' and giving the full credit to the players.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team on a video call, while fans across the country celebrated the win as a national festival.

Former spinner Abdur Razzak noted that this victory strengthens Bangladesh's case for more Test opportunities against Australia in the future.

headline: Govt employees' new pay scale at final stage, may be announced anytime
summary: Prime Minister's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar confirms the government is committed to implementing the new pay scale for government employees.
details: The proposed new pay scale for government employees is in its final stages and could be announced at any moment, according to Prime Minister's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar.
Speaking to reporters at the Secretariat, the Principal Secretary stated that the government is fully committed to implementing the new pay scale.
During the briefing, he was also questioned about the rising prices of essential commodities in the market.
He acknowledged existing market problems and stated that the government is actively working to resolve them.
Sattar noted that the production chain had been somewhat disrupted, potentially due to issues related to fuel and electricity, but assured that these would be resolved.
caption:
New pay scale for government employees is almost here!

The proposed new pay scale for government employees is in its final stages and could be announced at any moment, according to Prime Minister's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar.

Speaking to reporters at the Secretariat, the Principal Secretary stated that the government is fully committed to implementing the new pay scale.

During the briefing, he was also questioned about the rising prices of essential commodities in the market.

He acknowledged existing market problems and stated that the government is actively working to resolve them.

Sattar noted that the production chain had been somewhat disrupted, potentially due to issues related to fuel and electricity, but assured that these would be resolved.
